tools.name: counterpart_print_route
tools.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1), Bambu: how this server reaches the printer for prints and for Stop/Pause/Resume. route is "lan" (the local network through FULU's BambuNetwork bridge), "cloud" (Bambu Cloud through FULU's bridge) or "developer" (the local network straight to a printer in LAN Only + Developer Mode, whose Pause, Resume and Stop need no Bambu app). options lists each with its label, whether it can be chosen here (and why not) and what controls do on it; choices lists the ids that can be chosen. mode and type are BAMBU_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_MODE and BAMBU_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_TYPE as resolved. Pass route to change it: the change applies to the next print and control at once, and is saved to the .env file in this server's working directory when that file exists (savedTo; null otherwise). Sends nothing to the printer.

tools.name: counterpart_diagnostics
tools.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1): this server's own diagnostics for a bug report, as files for the client to add to its export: the configured printer (kind, host, model, serial, connection; firmware is not read), this server's settings, slicer path and version, CAD runtime status, recent tool errors, this run's stderr log (printer connection messages, Bambu MQTT included). The Bambu network plug-in logs are not included. Redaction fails closed: configured secrets go in their encoded forms, JSON is redacted by key, and any log line that names a secret is withheld whole; serial numbers, error codes and whether a secret is set stay. Names, contents and notes stay within max_bytes; anything missing is listed in notes. Contacts no printer.

tools.name: counterpart_print_record
tools.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1): read a bounded persistent per-job flight record from disk, including dispatched SHA-256, selected mapping, timestamped allowlisted printer-report changes, expected sliced layer geometry and sampled camera evidence. Survives restart. No printer connection, polling or controls. Firmware FINISH is separate from physical unknown/consistent/suspect_no_growth/suspect_no_extrusion. Inspect pending visual assessment requests with the client worker; clear empty-footprint observations can flag no extrusion without an empty-bed reference. Missing history is unavailable, never fetched from the printer.

tools.name: counterpart_discover_printers
tools.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1): printers on the local network. Bambu Lab printers from their own SSDP announcements (UDP 2021), with serial, model (as bambu_model names it), name and firmware; OctoPrint, Klipper (Moonraker) and PrusaLink hosts from their Bonjour adverts (dns-sd on macOS, avahi-browse on Linux), with host and port. Listens for duration_ms (default 4000). network is "unavailable" when another app holds the Bambu port. Never connects to or authenticates with a printer.

Pass serial to get the model it names. Sends nothing to a printer and returns no configured values.

tools.name: counterpart_propose_filaments
tools.description: Counterpart contract (counterpart/1): which loaded spool prints each of a model's colours, before slicing. Reads the printer's filaments once (Bambu: the AMS and external spools). trays lists the spools a person may choose (label like "A2" or "External", a person-readable name, colour, material, feed, and the filament profile slice_stl takes). proposal gives each filament its nearest spool in OKLab colour with the asked-for material preferred, and a verdict: same-colour, closest (that colour isn't loaded; note says so), no-colour or none. One print feeds from one source: the AMS or the external spool. Pass chosen to check the person's spools against what is loaded now; mapping then lists every filament slot's spool (painted slots included), and problems says why a choice can't print.

tools.name: octoprint_request_api_key
tools.description: OctoPrint's Application Keys approval: instead of copying an API key, the person clicks Allow in OctoPrint. Call without request_id to start (host and port of the OctoPrint; app names this app in OctoPrint's prompt); the result has request_id and approve_url (OctoPrint's own approval page). Call again with request_id and wait_ms (up to 120000) to wait for the answer: status approved returns api_key and env {API_KEY}, the setting this server reads. This server keeps the request open between calls (OctoPrint drops one that isn't polled every 5 s) for up to 10 minutes. status unsupported means this OctoPrint has no Application Keys plugin: copy the key from OctoPrint's settings instead. OctoPrint allows 3 requests a minute, 5 in 10 minutes and 10 an hour. host and port name the OctoPrint being added; without port, a host given here uses port 80 (or its URL's own port), not this server's PRINTER_PORT.

tools.name: resume_print
tools.description: Resume a paused print. Resume reheats and moves the printer, so it only resumes a job this server instance inspected and started, and only when the printer freshly reports that job paused. Bambu re-reads the job over FTPS (or the plate G-code the printer extracted) and compares its SHA-256, and resumes over the same connection that printed. When the file cannot be re-read, a person confirms through MCP elicitation first (Bambu: only for files Bambu's plug-in placed; a file this server uploaded must re-read). Resume other jobs at the printer.

runtime_dir.description: Installed runtime directory. On macOS this defaults to ~/Library/Application Support/OrcaSlicer/macos-bridge/runtime. When run_bridge_probe=true, requires MCP_ALLOW_EXECUTABLE_ARG=1 to be accepted here.

platform.description: Platform to inspect. Defaults to the current Node.js platform.

bridge_command.description: Command that starts the FULU BambuNetwork bridge host for probing. Read from FULU_BAMBU_BRIDGE_COMMAND by default; requires MCP_ALLOW_EXECUTABLE_ARG=1 to be accepted here.

run_bridge_probe.description: When true, sends bridge.handshake, bridge.capabilities, and bridge.runtime_info to the bridge host.

tools.name: fulu_bambu_network_rpc
tools.description: Advanced FULU bridge RPC for BambuNetwork diagnostics and development. Read-only methods are allowed by default. Agent/session setup methods require allow_mutating_method=true. Raw print methods, printer messages, file transfers and unknown methods are refused because they would bypass the print safety gate; use print_3mf for checked printing.

bridge_command.description: Command that starts the FULU BambuNetwork bridge host. Defaults to FULU_BAMBU_BRIDGE_COMMAND; requires MCP_ALLOW_EXECUTABLE_ARG=1 to be accepted here.

method.description: FULU bridge method, e.g. bridge.handshake, bridge.runtime_info, net.get_user_print_info, net.start_print.

payload.description: JSON payload sent to the FULU bridge method.

allow_mutating_method.description: Required for the allowlisted agent/session setup methods. It never enables print, printer-message, or unknown methods.

bambu_model.description: Informational only. Raw FULU print RPC methods are disabled; use print_3mf.

tools.name: merge_vertices
tools.description: Merge vertices in an STL file that are closer than the specified tolerance.

stl_path.description: Path to the STL file to modify.

tolerance.description: Maximum distance between vertices to merge (in mm, default: 0.01).

tools.name: center_model
tools.description: Translate the model so its geometric center is at the origin (0,0,0).

stl_path.description: Path to the STL file to center.

tools.name: lay_flat
tools.description: Rotate the model so a face rests on the bed (Z=0), choosing the orientation with the least part and support volume per mm² of bed contact. A face counts only if nothing hangs below it. Returns the new STL path; structuredContent.laid_flat is false, with the input path, when no orientation qualifies.

stl_path.description: Path to the STL file to lay flat.

tools.name: design_guidance
tools.description: Read one piece of this MCP's design guidance by name: fdm_fit (when a part meets a real object or another part); fdm_flexures (when a part must flex, grip, snap, clip, spring, or hold something by bending); fdm_assembly (when a split, joint, insert or printed thread could improve the result); fdm_multicolor (when several colours or support materials share a print); fdm_after_slice (when a candidate has been sliced, before recommending it); fdm_capability (when a bridge or overhang decides the plan and no measured capability is at hand). The same texts as the prompts of those names, for a worker that has tools but not prompts. Read-only.

tools.name: cad_status
tools.description: Read the optional code-CAD runtime's readiness and pinned version. Never installs or downloads anything. When only this MCP's own engine files changed since the runtime was last verified (an update) and the installed runtime still matches the pinned lock exactly, it re-runs setup's confined build, STL and STEP round trip (about 15 to 20 seconds) and reports ready; a changed runtime still needs cad_setup with install: true.

tools.name: cad_setup
tools.description: Check the optional confined build123d runtime. With install: true, use uv to install pinned Python/packages in this MCP's data directory and prove a confined build plus STL/STEP round trip. On macOS, the data directory must be on an internal disk with file ownership enabled; external/network volumes are refused before installation. Native signatures are never modified. Never starts Blender, Fusion or a printer.

install.description: Install and verify the pinned optional runtime; false only checks it.

tools.name: cad_run
tools.description: Build parametric CAD headlessly in OS confinement. Read cad_design first: declare literal P = {...} and build() returning a build123d Shape. Supply script OR script_path; parameters overrides saved named values in one call before derived dimensions. Calls wait for the environment’s exclusive execution slot up to their own deadline and report queue_wait_ms. Each call creates a private immutable subfolder under allowed output_dir, never overwriting previous artifacts. The saved .py and .parameters.json are the recovery checkpoint even after cancellation. Returns independently measured geometry, STL/STEP, six orthographic renders, a perspective view and a contact sheet (with next: read the perspective view before the next change), the closest approach between every pair of solids (bodies), problems, what was checked and not checked, printed: whatever the script wrote with print(), capped at 4000 characters, so a design can report a number it computed, and, in solid mode, purpose and ready: the script's PURPOSE compiled into requirements and evaluated on its use() assembly (held objects, mounts, loads computed from the geometry, facing the user). valid means only that the exported geometry is sound; final: true is recorded only when the design is ready (final_refused says why not).

inputs.description: Explicit named files [{name, path}]. Content-addressed immutable input bundles are reused; snapshot_bytes_added/reused report storage. Only the selected declared bundle is exposed to build() as INPUTS[name]; nested path is declared for remote path policy.

mode.description: solid returns build123d B-rep with STL/STEP; mesh returns trimesh.Trimesh with STL and an explicit unavailable STEP.

script.description: Python source declaring literal named P parameters and build() returning a Shape.

script_path.description: Allowed saved .py checkpoint to rebuild or edit instead of resending script.

parameters.description: Overrides for names already declared in P; saved values are retained.

output_dir.description: Existing allowed directory; a unique immutable run subfolder is created beneath it.

name.description: Plain file stem for STL, STEP, Python and parameter artifacts.

role.description: What this run is: "design" (the default) for the design itself, or "check" for a fit check part, a reference export or any other run that must never become the model. A check run is never selected as final, evaluates no PURPOSE, and its receipt says role: "check".

final.description: Mark the selected result. The protected cad-result.json records this flag and all returned validation; select completed final records after restart and still inspect valid/checks.

timeout_ms.description: Total queue wait, preparation, execution and inspection deadline. Default 120000 ms; cancellation kills the dispatched process group.

tools.name: cad_examples
tools.description: The code engine's cookbook: worked build123d designs from simple to complex, each modelled on the best bought version of the thing, with its concept, published sizes and script. Without arguments, lists them by purpose (name, title, use_for: the requests it suits, the pattern it shows, the product it is modelled on): choose by use_for before choosing a mechanism. With name, returns that example's record and full script to adapt. Read-only; starts no process.

name.description: An example's name from the list; omit to list them.

tools.name: cad_check_fit
tools.description: Check two allowed watertight manifold STL meshes in millimetres. Applies only the explicit rigid transform to reference: XYZ rotation in degrees about the origin, then translation. Never silently scales a scan. Reports Boolean interference volume and minimum surface gap (zero on contact/intersection), plus a clearance verdict; intentional support contact also has zero gap. Like cad_run, a call waits for the environment's exclusive execution slot up to its timeout_ms and reports queue_wait_ms, so several checks may be sent at once. Fails rather than guessing for open meshes or excessive triangle workload.

model.description: Allowed watertight manifold model STL in millimetres.

reference.description: Allowed reference/scan STL in millimetres; never rescaled implicitly.

transform.description: Rigid transform applied only to reference: XYZ rotation about origin, then translation.

clearance_mm.description: Required global minimum surface gap; intentional support contact has zero gap.

timeout_ms.description: Total queue wait, preparation, execution and inspection deadline. Default 120000 ms; cancellation kills the dispatched process group.

tools.name: blender_mcp_status
tools.description: Inspect Blender MCP configuration or connect and discover the remote server's tools. Lists tool names and summaries; pass tool_names for the full input schemas of the tools you will call. Connecting does not edit the scene; use get_scene_info through blender_mcp_call to check the Blender addon.

connect.description: Initialize the configured stdio MCP server and discover its tools (default false).

tool_names.description: Return full input schemas for these discovered tools, such as ["execute_blender_code"].

include_schemas.description: Return every discovered tool's full definition (large; default false).

timeout_ms.description: Total connection and discovery deadline in milliseconds; defaults to BLENDER_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 120000.

tools.name: blender_mcp_call
tools.description: Call a discovered tool on the configured Blender MCP server, preserving its full MCP content and errors. Discover tool schemas with blender_mcp_status first; execute_blender_code accepts Python code and user_prompt. Calls can modify the active Blender scene and are never automatically retried.

tool_name.description: Exact name advertised by Blender MCP, such as get_scene_info or execute_blender_code.

arguments.description: Arguments matching the remote tool's discovered input schema. Preserve the user's own words in user_prompt when the remote tool requests it.

timeout_ms.description: Total connection, discovery, and tool deadline in milliseconds; defaults to BLENDER_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 120000.

tools.name: blender_mcp_export_stl
tools.description: Export named objects from the live Blender scene to a new, verified STL for slicing. Writes world-space geometry with modifiers applied, without changing the scene, selection, or mode, and reports triangle count and bounding-box dimensions from the written file. Use this after editing or modelling through blender_mcp_call; Blender MCP's own export_scene writes GLB/FBX only. Requires standard Blender MCP and a shared local filesystem.

object_names.description: Blender object names to export together as one STL (mesh, curve, surface, metaball, or text objects).

output_path.description: New local .stl path. Its parent must exist; existing files are never overwritten.

apply_modifiers.description: Export the evaluated geometry with modifiers applied (default true).

scale.description: Multiply coordinates before writing (default 1). Slicers read STL units as millimetres, so use 1000 for a scene modelled in metres.

user_prompt.description: The user's own words, passed unchanged to Blender MCP.

timeout_ms.description: Total Blender request deadline in milliseconds; defaults to BLENDER_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 120000.

tools.name: blender_mcp_edit_model
tools.description: Import, edit, and export a local STL through standard Blender MCP with verified output and existing scene objects preserved. Requires a shared local filesystem and Blender Object Mode. Also supports a separately configured legacy executable bridge.

stl_path.description: Path to the local STL file

operations.description: Ordered operations: decimate:<ratio greater than 0 and at most 1>, remesh:<positive voxel size in STL units>, boolean_union:<STL path>. Legacy custom bridges define their own operations.

output_path.description: New local STL output path for standard MCP editing; defaults to a unique model-edited-<id>.stl beside the input. Its parent must exist and existing files are never overwritten. Reuse the preview's output_path when executing that plan.

user_prompt.description: The user's own words describing the edit, passed unchanged to Blender MCP.

timeout_ms.description: Total Blender request deadline in milliseconds; defaults to BLENDER_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 120000.

bridge_command.description: Legacy custom bridge executable override, not a standard MCP command. Per-call overrides require MCP_ALLOW_EXECUTABLE_ARG=1.

execute.description: Apply edits and export (true) or validate and return the prepared request without connecting (false, default).

tools.name: blender_mcp_setup
tools.description: Check or update the MCP for Blender add-on that the configured Blender bridge (BLENDER_MCP_COMMAND uvx, BLENDER_MCP_ARGS naming mcp-for-blender or blender-mcp) needs. Without update: which add-on file Blender loads, its protocol and the protocol the package expects, whether Blender is listening and the running add-on's own handshake. Changes nothing. With update: true, stages the add-on with the package's own installer (mcp-for-blender install-addon) at the inspected version, checks it, keeps the old file as a backup next to it and renames the new one into place. Never starts, stops or edits Blender; a running Blender uses the new add-on once it is re-enabled or restarted. A custom bridge returns supported false.

update.description: Replace the installed add-on with the package's own (default false: check only).

tools.name: fusion_mcp_setup
tools.description: Check or install what the Fusion bridge needs on macOS: Autodesk Fusion itself (found, never installed), the Fusion360MCP add-in from DMontgomery40/fusion360-mcp-server at 86a3016a5a5b (every file checked against its pinned SHA-256) set to run on startup, a login item that sets FUSION_MCP_PORT for Fusion however it is opened, and this server's FUSION_MCP_* settings. Without install: reports them and changes nothing. With install: true, installs what is missing and adds the missing settings to this server's own .env (after a copy of it), never rewriting one it already has. Never starts or quits Fusion; check the connection with fusion_mcp_status.

install.description: Install what is missing (default false: check only).

tools.name: fusion_mcp_status
tools.description: Check the Autodesk Fusion bridge: whether the Fusion MCP server is configured (by default DMontgomery40/fusion360-mcp-server@86a3016a5a5b, faust-machines' server with document binding; fusion_mcp_setup installs it), whether Fusion is running, whether its Fusion360MCP add-in answers on its port, and the server's tools and schemas. Reports responsive, state (starting/ready/unresponsive) and reason from a fresh no-op command probe capped at five seconds. No design is opened or edited. Failed probes clear connected; ready does not guarantee a later design operation succeeds. With launch: true and Fusion not running on this Mac, opens Autodesk Fusion and waits up to 90 s for the add-in.

launch.description: Open Autodesk Fusion when it is not running (macOS), then wait up to 90 s for the add-in (default false).

timeout_ms.description: Connection, discovery and command probe deadline, capped at 5000 ms; launch waiting is separate. The first uvx start may need a later retry after its initial download.

tools.name: fusion_mcp_call
tools.description: Call a discovered tool on the Fusion MCP server (create_sketch, extrude, fillet, set_parameter, export_stl, execute_code, and others), preserving its full MCP content and errors. Discover tool schemas with fusion_mcp_status first. Calls change the active Fusion design and are never automatically retried. Most tools need an active design: call fusion_mcp_new_design first.

tool_name.description: Exact name advertised by the Fusion MCP server.

arguments.description: Arguments matching the remote tool's discovered input schema. Fusion lengths are in centimetres unless a tool says otherwise.

timeout_ms.description: Deadline in milliseconds; defaults to FUSION_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 180000.

tools.name: fusion_mcp_new_design
tools.description: Open a new parametric design document in Fusion, so the Fusion tools have an active design. Fusion must already have some document open: at the pinned faust-machines commit no tool works from Fusion's home screen (issue #12).

timeout_ms.description: Deadline in milliseconds; defaults to FUSION_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 180000.

tools.name: fusion_mcp_export
tools.description: Export the active Fusion design into output_dir as <name>.stl (export_stl), <name>.f3d (export_f3d) and <name>.parameters.json (the design's user parameters), and return their absolute paths. The STL is checked as a finite triangle mesh and its size compared with the Fusion body to report its units. Existing files are never overwritten. Fusion and this server must share the computer's file system.

output_dir.description: Existing absolute directory for the three files.

name.description: Base file name without a path or extension, such as "bracket".

body_name.description: Body to export as the STL. Optional when the design has exactly one visible solid body.

timeout_ms.description: Deadline in milliseconds; defaults to FUSION_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS or 180000.

instructions: When designing or editing a model to print, apply the fdm_design prompt and the fdm_slicing prompt. Add fdm_fit whenever a part meets a real object or another part, to choose each fit by what that interface has to do. Add fdm_flexures whenever a part must flex, grip, snap, clip, spring, or hold something by bending. Add fdm_multicolor when several colours or support materials share a print, fdm_assembly when a split, joint or printed fastener could help, and fdm_after_slice as a separate review turn after a candidate has been sliced, before presenting the manufacturing recommendation. Read guidance://fdm/capability-guidance when a bridge or overhang is consequential and there is no sufficiently specific measured capability available. Read guidance://fdm/fit-by-function for the same fit guidance as the fdm_fit prompt, in resource form. A worker that has tools but not prompts reads the same guidance with the design_guidance tool (fdm_fit, fdm_flexures, fdm_assembly, fdm_multicolor, fdm_after_slice, fdm_capability). When monitoring a print, firmware layer counters do not verify deposition. Follow physical.assessment requests at the first layer and later checkpoints: fetch counterpart_print_record with frame_format images, inspect the expected footprint with the client vision worker, then submit counterpart_print_assess. A clear empty footprint after attempted printing is suspect_no_extrusion; no baseline is required for that direct observation. Dark/occluded/unlocatable views are unknown. Never announce a first layer is down from counters alone. Do not stop or pause automatically. For headless dimensioned designs and parameter edits, read the cad_design prompt before using cad_run.
